component.name: Reverblabr
component.summary: Capture, process and route audio on your desktop

description.p: Reverblabr takes the sound of an application, a microphone or everything your computer plays, sends it through the effects you put together, and plays it, records it or hands it to other applications as a microphone of its own. You build each chain on a canvas, block by block, and hear every change while it plays.
Capturing an application does not move it: it goes on playing where it was playing, and Reverblabr listens alongside. Nothing is changed in the application, and nothing has to be installed into it.
What you can do with it:

ul.li: Make a call or a stream sound better: take the noise out of a voice, even out its level and shape its tone.
Record the sound of one application, or of a microphone and an application side by side, to WAV, FLAC, MP3, Opus and more.
Turn a quiet programme up, a loud one down, or duck the music whenever someone speaks.
Shape the sound for one ear or both, with gain that depends on pitch and level, and move high or low sounds into a range that is easier to hear.
Make virtual outputs and microphones that other applications can use.
Use LV2 and LADSPA plugins beside the built-in effects, and CLAP and VST3 plugins where the package supports them.
Keep sessions running with the window closed, from the system tray, from global shortcuts or from the command line.

description.p: A package for Fedora 45, and an AppImage:

ul.li: a package for Fedora 45, beside the one for Fedora 44: a package built for one Fedora doesn't start on the other;
an AppImage, one file that runs without being installed on other distributions with Plasma 6 and PipeWire, without Auto Run, timers, KRunner, the panel widget and virtual devices for all users;
the waveform no longer says "No crossing found" for a moment after it has found one.

description.p: Reverblabr in your language, and a Settings window:

ul.li: the window, its notifications, the panel widget and the command-line tool in fourteen more languages: German, Spanish, French, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Polish, Japanese, Korean, Simplified and Traditional Chinese, Ukrainian, Dutch and Turkish;
a Settings window, where the language, the appearance and Auto Run are chosen.
sessions built on a canvas from sources, effects, meters and outputs, changed while they play, with undo;
capture of an application, a microphone or everything the computer plays, without moving what is captured;
more than twenty built-in effects, from volume, equalisers and dynamics to noise and hum removal, reverb, echo and pitch shifting;
blocks that shape the sound for each ear, set up from an audiogram, and move sounds into a range that is easier to hear;
peak, RMS and VU meters, a waveform and a spectrum at any point in a session;
recording to WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3, Opus and Vorbis, and to M4A where the system's FFmpeg can write it, with a Files tab to play back, rename and tag recordings;
LV2 and LADSPA plugins, and CLAP and VST3 plugins where the package supports them, each in a process of its own;
virtual outputs and microphones that other applications can use;
a background engine that keeps sessions running with the window closed, a system tray icon, desktop notifications, global shortcuts and a command-line tool;
packages for Fedora 44, Ubuntu 26.04 and Debian testing, and a Flatpak.

description.p: The first version, not yet released. It has:

ul.li: sessions built on a canvas from sources, effects, meters and outputs, with undo;
capture of an application, a microphone or the whole system, without moving what is captured;
built-in effects, from volume, equalisers and dynamics to noise and hum removal, reverb, pitch shifting and blocks that shape the sound for each ear;
recording to WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3, Opus, Vorbis and M4A, with a Files tab to find, play back, rename and tag recordings;
LV2, CLAP and LADSPA plugins, each in a process of its own;
virtual outputs and microphones;
a background engine that keeps sessions running with the window closed, a system tray icon, desktop notifications, global shortcuts and a command-line tool.
